Instrument (EN): Intuitive Eating Scale-3 — French-Canadian psychometric adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Intuitive eating: general factor and four specific factors — unconditional permission to eat; eating for physical rather than emotional reasons; reliance on hunger/satiety cues; body-food choice congruence (four-factor / bifactor ESEM).
Research provenance: Maïano C, Tylka TL, Aimé A, Swami V, Eating Disorders, published online 2026-07-05, DOI 10.1080/10640266.2026.2680097. New respondent-language French translation, N772 French-speaking Canadian adults; split-half exploratory then bifactor ESEM; gender invariance and no detected age/BMI measurement bias; composite reliability and convergent/concurrent validity reported.
DB locales: Research only; no FR published app.assessment_versions in live Holistic House. Same scale family as previously registered in research master IES3 EN-US original (key ies3-tylka2024-enus12-original), IES3 Turkish (key ies3-mengicelik2026-tr12) and Brazilian Portuguese; NOT independent scale family.
EN form: Not a new EN adaptation; original US EN IES3 already indexed as ies3-tylka2024-enus12-original.
RU form: No independently verified RU-RU IES3 respondent adaptation from this study.
ES form: No independently verified ES-language IES3 respondent adaptation from this study.
Other translations: FR-CA: new translated French respondent edition empirically validated in this study on N772 adults, distinct from interface language. Older IES2 does NOT have interchangeable wording/scoring.
Target population: 772 French-speaking Canadian adults, split into exploratory and confirmatory subsamples. Not representative national eating-disorder norms.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Author statement permitting unmodified IES-3 use does not by itself resolve rights to French translation, publisher-formatted item reproduction, scoring, commercial SaaS, or potential derivative modifications. Obtain translated-form written clearance and audit final items/scorer.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. 12-item French-Canadian respondent form is studied (not merely UI localization), same IES3 instrument family; eating-related vulnerability safeguards. No questions, normative scores, automated interpretations, or live app changes.

Instrument (EN): Sleep, Circadian Rhythms, and Mood (SCRAM) questionnaire — Korean validated adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Three distinct factors: Good Sleep; Morningness; Depressed Mood. No clinically validated diagnostic threshold or reliable general one-factor total.
Research provenance: Chung S, Shahrier MA, Chronobiology International, published 2026-09-11, DOI 10.1080/07420528.2026.2732186. Korean respondent-language questionnaire validation, N528 analyzed of 600 online general-population respondents; EFA N265, CFA N263, CFI .987, TLI .985, RMSEA .062, SRMR .049; domain alphas .876, .873, .924, total alpha .698.
DB locales: Not in published Supabase as Korean app locale or instrument version; new source-level language edition, no site activation.
EN form: Publication is English-language but this study does not independently establish a validated new English respondent version.
Other translations: KO-KR: Korean translation explicitly developed/tested in sample; total-score alpha .698 discourages assuming unidimensional total; distinct 3 subscale factors.
Target population: Korean online general-population adults, 528 analyzed after 600 recruitment; EFA 265/CFA 263 same parent cohort; not a psychiatric patient standardization sample.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Confirm original SCRAM owner and Korean translator permissions for full Korean response items, digital commercial SaaS distribution, subscale scoring, interpretation and derivative adaptations. Journal abstract not a commercial license.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Validated Korean respondent edition, 3 dimensions; combined total alpha=.698, not substitute for sleep/mood diagnostic screen. Mood/depression domains require safety protocol; no reproduction or deployment.

Instrument (EN): Sleeping Pills Receptivity and Involuntariness Scale-6 — original Korean-sample study
Scales / measured domains (EN): Two 3-item factors: perceived involuntary nature of insomnia; receptivity/acceptance of hypnotic medication. Attitudes, not medication effectiveness or indication.
Research provenance: Chung S, Shahrier MA, Nature and Science of Sleep 2025-09-26, DOI 10.2147/NSS.S550404. Original scale development in N600 general Korean online respondents, EFA N300 CFA N300, CFI/TLI .99, RMSEA .02, omega .80. Article open under CC BY-NC 4.0; commercial item reproduction requires express licence.
DB locales: Research-only key; no distinct SPRIS6 published in app.assessment_versions as of 2026-10-24 read-only audit.
EN form: English article/abstract and published English item labels do not prove a psychometrically tested EN respondent questionnaire.
Other translations: Korean population was tested, but exact finalized respondent-language form, response anchors and their usage rights are NOT independently confirmed; do not mark KO-KR as language-validated solely from country/population.
Target population: 600 general Korean participants, split EFA/CFA 300/300; measure of attitudes about insomnia/hypnotics, NOT a clinical medication decision or efficacy test.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Dove Medical Press article under CC BY-NC 4.0; commercial use prohibited by default, requires explicit developer/publisher permission for digital site questionnaire, responses, scoring and translations. Clinician oversight for medication-related messaging.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. Do NOT recommend starting, stopping, changing hypnotics from these scores. Korean sample is not automatically a Korean-language validated form; authorized original questions and language remain pending.

Instrument (EN): Adaptive Cognition About Sleep-2 — two-item short derivative of ACBS-6
Scales / measured domains (EN): Adaptive cognitions concerning sleep (two selected ACBS-6 cognition items 2 and 4); excludes original ACBS-6 adaptive-behavior subscale.
Research provenance: Chung S et al, Sleep Medicine Research, 2026, DOI 10.17241/smr.2026.03874. Four Korean adult online datasets: derivation general-population N600; validation general N600, insomnia N600, insomnia+hypnotics N500 (N2300 across samples). Spearman–Brown split-half reliability .59-.75; inverse ISI correlation r=-.14 to -.23; proposed mediation not observed.
DB locales: New ultra-short derived edition of ACBS-6 (other ACBS-6 edition keyed acbs6-lee2026-kr6-insomnia-followup); not another independent scale family, no existing published ACS-2 live app key.
EN form: Publication in English not evidence of independently validated English respondent-language ACS2 items.
RU form: No independently verified Russian respondent edition.
ES form: No independently verified Spanish respondent edition.
Other translations: Korean adult samples; exact administered question language not confirmed. Study evaluated psychometrics of two-item form, but do not claim validated KO-KR translated instrument purely from sample country.
Target population: Korean adults N600 general derivation + independent validation groups N600 general/N600 with insomnia/N500 with insomnia and hypnotic use; subgroup/response overlap not independently audited.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Research paper and two-item shortening confer no automatic rights to original ACBS-6 adapted questions, commercial digital delivery, translated wording, screening recommendations or scorer. Written original developer authorization needed.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Very brief instrument with reliability only .59-.75; not full ACBS-6 factor replacement, no clinical insomnia diagnosis. Korean respondent language and digital rights pending. No app release.
